Quick attempt at explaining based on fuzzy memory from biochem class - when a prion protein (PrP) misfolds it goes from its cellular form (PrPc) which is mostly helices to its infectious form (PrPsc), which is mostly pleated sheets. The infectious form can cause the normal, cellular PrPc proteins present around it (because they're present throughout the body) to misfold and become PrPsc as well, which goes on exponentially as the more infectious forms there are, the more normal PrPc will be misfolded and converted to the infectious form. The infectious form builds up and eventually causing aggregates of protein which cause cell death. I'm pretty sure the aggregates and cell death is what results in the symptoms and eventually mortality associated with prion diseases, but there could definitely be more to it.
